title: SQL Day 7 — Dates, Time Analysis & Period KPIs
description: Convert date fields into useful reporting periods and analyze order timing with SQL date functions.

topics.title: Date Components
topics.business_skill: Extract year, month, and day information for reporting.

teaching.teacher: ## Date parts\nDate functions vary by SQL engine, but the business goal is the same: derive calendar components from a date.
teaching.explain: Year and month are common reporting dimensions; use engine-specific functions such as YEAR() and MONTH() where supported.
teaching.detailedlearning: Keep the original date available when row-level detail is needed and derive reporting fields separately.
teaching.expose: Date transformations should preserve the underlying date meaning.
teaching.example: SELECT order_id, YEAR(order_date) AS order_year, MONTH(order_date) AS order_month FROM orders;
teaching.business_question: The BI manager wants order year and month for each transaction.
teaching.expected_sql: SELECT order_id, order_date, YEAR(order_date) AS order_year, MONTH(order_date) AS order_month FROM orders;

topics.title: Month-Level Aggregation
topics.business_skill: Build monthly sales and profit trends.

teaching.teacher: ## Monthly KPI\nGroup transactions by the derived month period and aggregate measures.
teaching.explain: The grouping key must identify a complete reporting period, normally year plus month.
teaching.detailedlearning: Grouping only by month number can mix January across multiple years.
teaching.expose: A monthly trend should not accidentally combine different years.
teaching.example: SELECT YEAR(order_date) AS order_year, MONTH(order_date) AS order_month, SUM(sales) AS sales FROM orders GROUP BY YEAR(order_date), MONTH(order_date);
teaching.business_question: The sales director wants monthly sales and profit.
teaching.expected_sql: SELECT YEAR(order_date) AS order_year, MONTH(order_date) AS order_month, SUM(sales) AS sales, SUM(profit) AS profit FROM orders GROUP BY YEAR(order_date), MONTH(order_date);

topics.title: Date Ranges & Relative Periods
topics.business_skill: Filter transactions to business reporting windows.

teaching.teacher: ## Date filters\nUse explicit date boundaries for reliable period filtering; prefer half-open ranges when timestamps are involved.
teaching.explain: A period request such as 'January' should become a precise start and end condition.
teaching.detailedlearning: Avoid ambiguous text date comparisons and remember that timestamps can contain time components.
teaching.expose: Date filtering errors often come from unclear boundaries.
teaching.expected_sql: SELECT order_id, order_date, sales FROM orders WHERE order_date >= '2025-01-01' AND order_date < '2025-02-01';

topics.title: Order Date vs Reporting Period
topics.business_skill: Analyze order timing and reporting periods using the order date field.

teaching.teacher:
## Order dates and reporting periods
An order date tells you when a transaction was placed. A reporting period groups those dates into a year, month, quarter, or other business interval.
teaching.explain: Use the available order_date field consistently when building time-based reports. This orders dataset does not contain a ship_date field.
teaching.detailedlearning: Extract date components for grouping and use explicit inclusive-start, exclusive-end boundaries for date ranges. Keep the underlying date field at transaction grain.
teaching.expose: A month label is useful for display, but year and month must both be retained when aggregating across multiple years.
teaching.example: SELECT order_id, order_date, strftime('%Y-%m', order_date) AS order_period FROM orders;
teaching.business_question: The operations analyst wants order-level dates and reporting periods for monthly analysis.
teaching.expected_sql: SELECT order_id, order_date, strftime('%Y-%m', order_date) AS order_period FROM orders;

topics.title: Date-Driven KPI Reporting
topics.business_skill: Combine time dimensions with business metrics.

teaching.teacher: ## Time-based KPI\nA useful time report combines a stable period grain with the measures stakeholders actually monitor.
teaching.explain: Define the period, aggregate the KPIs, and order chronologically.
teaching.detailedlearning: Use year plus month or another unambiguous period key; never rely on alphabetical month names for chronology.
teaching.expose: Correct chronology is part of report correctness.
teaching.example: SELECT YEAR(order_date) AS yr, MONTH(order_date) AS mo, SUM(sales) AS sales, SUM(profit) AS profit FROM orders GROUP BY YEAR(order_date), MONTH(order_date) ORDER BY yr, mo;
teaching.business_question: The CEO wants a chronological monthly sales and profit trend.
teaching.expected_sql: SELECT YEAR(order_date) AS yr, MONTH(order_date) AS mo, COUNT(*) AS orders, SUM(sales) AS sales, SUM(profit) AS profit FROM orders GROUP BY YEAR(order_date), MONTH(order_date) ORDER BY yr, mo;
